leads.summary: Eager mise pin failure now aborts user finalization before later tools and defaults
leads.consequence: If mise cannot fetch the first package (for example offline during ISO setup), the installer exits 1 without writing codex and the caller's bash -eE stops before gh, remaining wrappers, application refresh, default browser and mailto handler, and finalize-user marker. The old wrapper generator wrote stubs without installing their packages. Subsequent finalization must be retried when the network is available.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus F1 (eager mise use -g aborts user setup); published

leads.summary: Open PR #12329's Remove Agents cannot recognize any new exec-only launcher
leads.consequence: Both unstacked diffs apply to one tree, but #12329 compares the entire launcher to only the old mutating templates. For an installed codex with the new wrapper, --check fails, the Remove > Agents row hides, and a direct removal says it is not an Omarchy-managed CLI. Applies to every generic agent in that PR whose wrapper is regenerated by this PR; Hermes has its own marker. Its remove-agent-test also tries the now eager installer before it can exercise this predicate.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; #12329 owned_wrapper matches only old mutating templates (sol/pr-12329.diff:39-54, PR open); published in Details

leads.summary: An orphaned OpenClaw gateway unit blocks installation despite a missing CLI
leads.consequence: An enabled or merely existing openclaw-gateway.service makes --check and --now succeed without installing a missing openclaw executable, and disables the Install > AI menu entry. Selecting it as default records openclaw, but omarchy-agent:49-52 rejects it as not installed. Next run remains blocked until the stale unit is removed manually; a broken executable on PATH has the analogous false-positive because command -v does not run it.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus F5 (leftover gateway unit); published in More findings

leads.summary: Remove Preinstalls leaves the new Cursor Agent and Muse mise stubs behind
leads.consequence: The removal command only recognizes those two Omarchy-owned files by a line starting mise use -g, whereas the new generated wrappers start exec mise x. These two tools remain executable after Remove Preinstalls claims success, despite the explicit intent to preserve only user-managed launchers. Other fixed-name wrappers are deleted unconditionally, so this is exactly cursor-agent and muse; restoring/re-removing does not fix the missed predicates.

leads.summary: The wrapper migration discards a user's added lines and can repurpose a different package
leads.consequence: Unlike the older migration's exact whole-file shape check, this scanner matches any short readable file with a standalone mise use -g line and separately extracts an exec line without checking they refer to the same package. It reruns mise use for the first package, then overwrites the file with a wrapper for that package and the separately parsed bin, dropping custom environment exports or other commands; a user-owned script with a different package in its exec now executes a different program. Migration runs under bash -euo pipefail, so a failed install leaves the changed wrappers before it and aborts pending migrations without a completion marker.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus F2 (migration rewrites user wrappers); published in More findings

leads.summary: Two added binaries fail the repository-wide bin style test
leads.consequence: test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh:7-9 rejects raw command -v in every bin command outside the allowed helper families, so the shell test suite fails immediately on both newly added binaries even though their focused tests pass. Use omarchy-cmd-present for both lookups or update the rule deliberately.

leads.summary: Open PR #13781's stub-restoration migration fails after this PR makes stub generation eager
leads.consequence: The later migration sources install/user/mise.sh to recreate missing lazy stubs and defines a no-op mise shell function, but the installer it invokes is a subprocess and calls real mise use -g. A missing package or unavailable network now stops restoration before gh or later stubs and leaves the migration pending; the combined PR's kept stub-restoration test fails immediately. This is not a stacked PR; patch applied without conflicts.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; #13781 migration sources install/user/mise.sh and calls command omarchy-mise-install; mise() function not visible to subprocess (sol/pr-13781.diff:13-33); Opus also confirmed in self-check C35; published in Details

leads.summary: OpenClaw web app loses its icon when a user-installed CLI causes the package to be skipped
leads.consequence: Running the public installer with a PATH OpenClaw and no pacman package skips that package, but passes the package-only /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/control-ui/apple-touch-icon.png as the desktop icon. omarchy-webapp-install treats missing local icon paths as theme names, strips the filename to apple-touch-icon and writes Icon=apple-touch-icon, leaving no icon installed by this flow while reporting success (unless some unrelated theme already supplies an icon with that name). Install > AI's disabled predicate may conceal the action, but direct command callers still reach it.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; opus/followup-1-openclaw-icon.md, run plan4/runs/20261001T043026Z-3f3dd9b1; CLI-only; published in More findings

leads.summary: The mise up failure message misdiagnoses a normal release cooldown
leads.consequence: At mise v2026.9.14, `mise up` is the upgrade alias; a newer release hidden by minimum_release_age produces an upstream warning, but with no eligible updates the command returns Ok(). The new Omarchy warning never fires for that normal case. If mise up does return nonzero, this script often tells users to adjust cooldown despite another cause (such as download/install failure) and swallows that failure from the update pipeline.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus F6 (message misattributes failure to cooldown); published

leads.summary: The retained old-migration test now tries to install impossible fixture package names
leads.consequence: It still runs migration 1787573629 with the real omarchy-mise-install and invented backend specs such as aqua:some/other. This PR changes that callee from writing wrappers to invoking real mise use -g first, so the test fails before any assertions or its customization checks, instead of validating the new migration. Stub the mise executable, not omarchy-mise-install, with an argv-logging fake.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus F4 (quiet-migration test calls real mise use); published

leads.summary: #11973's subsequent migration test fails against the new wrapper format
leads.consequence: Open #11973 adds an additional migration (1789490499) after this PR's 1789200000 rewrite. The later migration correctly finds no old mutating wrapper, but #11973's test still insists on a `mise use -g --quiet` line. Both diffs patch together cleanly and the combined test fails; update the later test/migration expectation when sequencing these PRs.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; #11973 test greps for mise use -g --quiet (sol/pr-11973.diff:88-96); published in Details

leads.summary: Two shipped documents still promise the removed lazy-install and zero-age update behaviour
leads.consequence: The manual says first use of gh installs the CLI, but this PR moves its mise use to provisioning/refresh and the wrapper itself only calls mise x. The update process table still describes omarchy-update-mise as intentionally forcing MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0, directly contrary to the new implementation. Fix both separate documents with the new lifecycle/age policy.
leads.triage: corroborated_partial; docs/update-process.md in F6 published; manual/18 lazy-stub wording covered by F1 report, not separately published

leads.summary: Open #13296 changes the package to a seed, contradicting package-as-ready presence
leads.consequence: If both PRs are reconciled but package-as-present remains, package-only machines pass this PR's OpenClaw --check even though #13296 requires a running user-owned runtime and a PATH pointer. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** `omarchy-mise-install` now exits 1 when `mise use -g` cannot download the tool, so offline user setup and the new migration stop.

### Writing a wrapper now needs the network

`install/user/mise.sh` runs under `bash -eE`, so one failed download stops `omarchy-provision-user` partway. Migration 1789200000 calls the same installer, so offline `omarchy-migrate` stops and the old wrapper stays.

**Suggested change:** Write the wrapper first and only warn if `mise use -g` fails (`mise x` installs on first run); have the migration only rewrite files.

<details><summary>Reproducer: user setup (fails at 58daba3)</summary>

install/user/mise.sh, sourced the way run_logged sources it (`bash -eE`), with a mise that cannot download anything.

Save as `test/shell.d/user-setup-offline-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/user-setup-offline-test.sh` from the repository root. mise is stubbed inside the test; nothing is downloaded.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

mock_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
test_home="$test_tmp/home"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin" "$test_home"

# A first boot or ISO install with no network yet: mise answers settings
# calls, but anything that has to download a tool fails.
cat >"$mock_bin/mise" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
case $1 in
  use | install | x | exec)
    echo "mise ERROR failed to fetch versions: network unreachable" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac
exit 0
SH
# Not under test here, and it reaches pacman.
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$mock_bin/omarchy-install-hermes-cli"
chmod +x "$mock_bin"/*

export PATH="$mock_bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH"
export HOME="$test_home"

# Sourced exactly as run_logged does it, so a non-zero exit here aborts
# omarchy-provision-user before the default browser, the mailto handler, the
# first-install migration markers and the finalize-user marker.
status=0
bash -eE -c 'source "$1"' bash "$ROOT/install/user/mise.sh" >"$test_tmp/out" 2>&1 || status=$?

wrappers=$(find "$test_home/.local/bin" -maxdepth 1 -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
(( status == 0 )) ||
  fail "user setup finishes without network" "exit status $status, $wrappers wrappers written
$(cat "$test_tmp/out")"
pass "user setup finishes without network ($wrappers wrappers written)"
```

```
not ok - user setup finishes without network
```

Output at 31bd80d (merge base), exit status 0:

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: migration (fails at 58daba3)</summary>

migrations/1789200000.sh run the way omarchy-migrate runs it (`bash -euo pipefail`), once with a mise that cannot download anything and once with a working mise over two wrappers the user changed. Migration 1789200000 does not exist at the merge base, so there is no base run.

Save as `test/shell.d/mise-wrapper-readonly-migration-edge-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/mise-wrapper-readonly-migration-edge-test.sh` from the repository root. mise is stubbed inside the test; nothing is downloaded.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1789200000.sh"
test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT

home="$test_dir/home"
bin_dir="$home/.local/bin"
mkdir -p "$bin_dir" "$test_dir/bin" "$test_dir/offline"

cat >"$test_dir/bin/mise" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
SH
cat >"$test_dir/offline/mise" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo "mise ERROR failed to fetch versions: network unreachable" >&2
exit 1
SH
chmod +x "$test_dir/bin/mise" "$test_dir/offline/mise"

# Run the way omarchy-migrate runs it.
run_migration() {
  HOME="$home" PATH="$1:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

failures=()

# The template omarchy-mise-install writes at the merge base.
cat >"$bin_dir/claude" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
export MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0
mise use -g --quiet "claude" || exit 1
exec mise x "claude" -- "claude" "$@"
EOF
chmod +x "$bin_dir/claude"

# 1. Rewriting a wrapper is a file edit. The earlier wrapper migrations
# (1784909971, 1787573629) did it without the network.
if ! run_migration "$test_dir/offline"; then
  failures+=("migration needs the network to rewrite a wrapper (exit non-zero, so omarchy-migrate stops and omarchy update aborts)")
fi
grep -q '^mise use -g' "$bin_dir/claude" &&
  failures+=("offline: the mutating claude wrapper is still in place")

# 2. Wrappers the user changed. 1787573629 leaves both alone (see
# mise-wrapper-quiet-migration-test.sh).
cat >"$bin_dir/customized" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
export MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0
export SOME_TOKEN=abc123
mise use -g --quiet "customized" || exit 1
exec mise x "customized" -- "customized" "$@"
EOF
cat >"$bin_dir/mismatched" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
mise use -g --quiet "one-package" || exit 1
exec mise x "another-package" -- "bin" "$@"
EOF
chmod +x "$bin_dir/customized" "$bin_dir/mismatched"
customized_before=$(<"$bin_dir/customized")
mismatched_before=$(<"$bin_dir/mismatched")

run_migration "$test_dir/bin" || failures+=("migration failed with a working mise")

[[ $(<"$bin_dir/customized") == "$customized_before" ]] ||
  failures+=("a generated wrapper a user added a line to is regenerated without that line")
[[ $(<"$bin_dir/mismatched") == "$mismatched_before" ]] ||
  failures+=("a wrapper whose two lines disagree is rewritten to a different package")

if (( ${#failures[@]} )); then
  printf -- '--- customized after migration\n%s\n--- mismatched after migration\n%s\n' \
    "$(<"$bin_dir/customized")" "$(<"$bin_dir/mismatched")" >&2
  for f in "${failures[@]}"; do printf 'not ok - %s\n' "$f" >&2; done
  exit 1
fi
pass "migration rewrites offline and leaves wrappers it did not write alone"
```

```
--- mismatched after migration
#!/bin/bash

not ok - a generated wrapper a user added a line to is regenerated without that line
not ok - a wrapper whose two lines disagree is rewritten to a different package
```
</details>

`omarchy-remove-preinstalls` finds the cursor-agent and muse wrappers by their `mise use -g` line. New and migrated wrappers lack it, so both stay.

**Suggested change:** Also match `^exec mise x "cursor-agent" --` and the muse form, as `omarchy-default-agent` now does.

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

**A leftover gateway unit counts as an OpenClaw install.** After the package is removed by hand, the unit file `openclaw gateway install` wrote stays, and `omarchy-openclaw-present` treats it as present. `omarchy-install-openclaw-cli --now` then installs nothing and the default agent is set to a missing `openclaw`. Run from the command line with no package but OpenClaw found on PATH or through such a unit, `omarchy-install-ai-openclaw` skips the install yet still passes the package's `/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/...` icon path, so the desktop entry gets `Icon=apple-touch-icon` with no icon installed, and it prints "OpenClaw has been installed." even when nothing was installed. **Suggested change:** for `--check`/`--now`, require the package or a runnable `openclaw` on PATH, and on the skip branch pick the icon from the installed `openclaw`.

**Migration rewrites wrappers it did not write.** Any file of 1 KiB or less in `~/.local/bin` with a quoted `mise use -g` line and an exec line is regenerated, dropping a user's added lines and taking the package from that line (see the migration reproducer). It also calls `omarchy-mise-install` rather than `omarchy-mise-install-bun`, so it installs claude and pi on CPUs the new SSE4.2 check rejects (CPU reproducer below). **Suggested change:** compare against the exact known templates, as migration 1787573629 does, and skip claude/pi when `omarchy-hw-cpu-sse4_2` fails.

**Existing tests fail at the head.** `bin-style-test.sh` rejects the raw `command -v` in `omarchy-hw-cpu-sse4_2` and `omarchy-openclaw-present` (use `omarchy-cmd-present`). `default-agent-test.sh` fails at "agent migration removes the obsolete Oh My Pi wrapper after opt-out", because migration 1785846769 also recognises wrappers by `mise use -g`. `mise-wrapper-quiet-migration-test.sh` now calls the real `mise use -g` on made-up packages. **Suggested change:** fix the two helpers and update the wrapper matchers and test stubs.

**Release age reverses a documented decision.** `docs/update-process.md` describes the `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0` override as "the point" of `omarchy-update-mise`, and #11886 is about writes on every run, not the cooldown. Without it, `omarchy update` holds back releases younger than mise's default (24h) and `mup` equals `mise up`. The new `if ! mise up` makes `omarchy-update-mise` always exit 0 (reproducer below; the rest is from source), and its message blames the cooldown, which on `mise up` normally just holds back the newest release with a warning. **Suggested change:** move the release-age change to its own PR and update the docs and manual if it is accepted.
</details>
